chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Walid (may God be pleased with them) narrated what they said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani (may God have mercy on them), who was with us on Hajj.

He said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) via my father, 'May I be your ransom! Our companions differ regarding the Sa'. Some say the Fitrah is calculated by the Sa of Medina, while others say by the Sa of Iraq.' He wrote back to me: 'The Sa is six Artals in the Medina measure and nine Artals in the Iraqi measure.' He said: And he informed me, saying: 'By weight, it is one thousand and seventy Dirhams.'

key_terms.الصَّاعُ: A unit of volume measurement used for Zakat and Fitrah
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: The alms tax given at the end of Ramadan (Zakat al-Fitr)

ai.seo_question: What is the exact measurement and weight value of the Sa for Fitrah according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) resolves the scholarly disagreement among companions regarding the specific volume of the 'Sa' used for Zakat al-Fitr, distinguishing between the Medina and Iraqi standards. He provides precise conversions—six Medina Artals or nine Iraqi Artals—and assigns a monetary weight of 1,070 Dirhams, reflecting the economic context of the time. This clarification underscores the Shia emphasis on adhering to specific, authenticated measurements for religious obligations to ensure uniformity and fairness in almsgiving.
